articles.title: El Bayer Leverkusen destroza al Union y Miguel Gutiérrez firma doblete de asistencias
articles.standfirst: Los de Carles Martínez se recuperan tras la derrota en el debut
articles.summary: Los de Carles Martínez se recuperan tras la derrota en el debut
articles.body: Tras arrancar la Bundesliga con el revés de la derrota a domicilio ante el debutante Elversberg, el Bayer Leverkusen del español Carles Martínez Novell se desquitó y goleó al Union Berlín (4-0) con una gran actuación de Miguel Gutiérrez. El ex del Girona y Nápoles dejó dos asistencias desde el costado izquierdo para arrancar la goleada. Los argentinos Ezequiel Fernández y Facundo Medina firmaron los tantos en la 'conexión hispana' del Bay Arena. Schick sentenció en la segunda parte y minutos más tardes, ya en el ecuador de la misma, asistió a Maza para certificar la aplastante victoria de un Leverkusen que se entona para confirmar que quiere volver a la Champions League tras no clasificar el pasado curso.

images.caption: Facundo Medina anota para el Leverkusen. EFE.

articles.title: El Dortmund levanta un 2-0 en contra antes de medirse al Villarreal en Champions
articles.standfirst: Guirassy, Fabio Silva y Hajdari (en propia) hicieron los tantos
articles.summary: Guirassy, Fabio Silva y Hajdari (en propia) hicieron los tantos
articles.body: A la espera el próximo martes del Villarreal en el inicio de la Liga de Campeones, el Borussia Dortmund se rehizo de un 2-0 en contra y una hora de juego muy por debajo del nivel, reaccionó a tiempo y logró una remontada épica, con el 2-3 del triunfo en el minuto 88 y en propia puerta del Hoffenheim. No era una simple revés. Y lo esquivó. El margen de error cuando pretendes jugar por ser ganador de la Bundesliga y compites con un equipo que falla tan poco como el Bayern Múnich, cada tropiezo es un paso atrás indudable, todavía más cuando es tan pronto, apenas la segunda jornada. Lo sorteó el grupo que dirige Nico Kovac, que sostiene el pleno de triunfos. No funcionó en una hora el conjunto amarillo, hasta entonces a contracorriente, un segundo más tarde, lejos del área rival y por momentos sostenido por su portero Gregor Kobel, el mejor de largo de su equipo, que lamentó la lesión del central Filippo Mané y que ya había sufrido ya varias ocasiones rivales, todavía con 0-0. El 1-0 fue un buen derechazo, con efecto de dentro hacia afuera, ajustado al otro palo, por Leon Avdullahu. Lo merecía ya el Hoffenheim, que fue más allá en el segundo tiempo, cuando Lemperle abrió aún más la distancia en el resultado con el 2-0, con apariencia de definitivo de no haber sido porque, de repente, Guirassy anotó el 2–1, con la sutileza de su definición en el área. Y el partido cambió. Tiene el Borussia Dortmund suficientes recursos para pasar de la nada al todo en unos instantes. Fabio Silva entró en el minuto 62. En el 66 cruzó su disparo, en su primera ocasión, para aportar el empate a su equipo, tan lejos unos minutos antes de la victoria y tan cerca de pronto. Un aviso al Hoffenheim… Y para el Villarreal, que lo visita el martes. La victoria, el 2-3, ya fue en el 87 en un gol en propia puerta del Hoffenheim. Triunfo del Dortmund, mucho mas preciado en el marcador que en el juego. No debe conformarse. Su pleno admite dudas.

images.caption: Fabio Silva anota para el Dortmund. EFE.

articles.title: Fofana, Félix Correia y Stassin se estrenan en la lista de García Plaza
articles.standfirst: 24 convocados para el partido de mañana frente al Espanyol
articles.summary: 24 convocados para el partido de mañana frente al Espanyol
articles.body: El Sevilla ha facilitado la lista de 24 convocados para la visita de mañana al Espanyol a las 21.00 horas. Tras sumar seis de seis en el arranque liguero y caer la pasada jornada ante el Atlético de Madrid, los andaluces buscan retomar la senda de la victoria. Los hispalenses se reforzaron el último día de mercado con tres incorporaciones: el belga Lucas Stassin, el portugués Félix Correia; y el fichaje sorpresa de Fofana, que llega cedido desde el Milan para reforzar la medular. Los tres forman parte de la convocatoria. Por lo demás, viaja todo el plantel a excepción de Marcao y de Rubén Vargas, que está pendiente de evolución por unas molestias en la rodilla. El suizo sufre una parameniscitis externa de la rodilla derecha, sobre la cual se le está realizando un tratamiento específico. La lista de 24 citados la conforman: Odysseas, Fran González, Sergio Recio, Iglesias, Carmona, Kike Salas, Iker Muñoz, Sangante, Castrín, Suazo, Julio Díaz, Agoumé, Guridi, Fofana, Manu Bueno, Kochorashvili, Félix, Miguel Sierra, Ejuke, Alfon, Peque, Isaac, Robbie Ure y Stassin.

images.caption: Fofana, en un entrenamiento con el Sevilla SEVILLA FC

articles.title: Y Julián sí fue esta vez a aplaudir a su afición
articles.standfirst: El argentino acudió con sus compañeros a agredecer a los 200 rojiblancos desplazados a Bilbao
articles.summary: El argentino acudió con sus compañeros a agredecer a los 200 rojiblancos desplazados a Bilbao
articles.body: Esta vez sí. Esta vez Julián no hizo como ante el Villarreal, día en el que el club le pidió que se marchara al vestuario en lugar de acudir a aplaudir a una hinchada que la tomó contra él después de todo lo acontecido sobre su situación contractual en el Atlético. Esta vez, y pese al duro 3-0 final, Julián fue uno más de los jugadores que se marcharon a la esquina en la que estaban los 200 aficionados del Atlético que apoyaron a los de Simeone pese a la primera derrota de la temporada Como ya sucedió desde el minuto de pisar el césped de San Mamés para el calentamiento, Julián estuvo arropado por los suyos. Con Musso y, sobre todo, el Cuti como lugartenientes el delantero acudió a aplaudir a una afición a la que espera volver a conquistar Julián Álvarez volvió a jugar un partido con el Atlético de Madrid. Tras lo sucedido en los últimos días del cierre de mercado y el culebrón que se ha vivido desde que saliera a la zona mixta a pedir una salida este verano, el argentino recibió los silbidos de la hinchada que se trasladó a Bilbao para animar al equipo de Diego Pablo Simeone en su partido ante el Athletic Club. A Julián Álvarez se le vio constantemente arropado por el Cuti Romero y Musso. El delantero se arropó en sus compatriotas en los momentos previos al duelo y, a la llegada del autobús a San Mamés, bajó junto con sus dos compañeros. También estuvo acompañados por ellos en varios momentos del calentamiento e incluso cuando saltó al terreno de juego en el minuto 58 recibió los mimos del guardameta Musso.

images.caption: Julián Álvarez, a su llegada a San Mamés junto con Musso y el Cuti Romero.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin says decision to leave former NFL players off LSU roster was in 'the best interest of the team and the university'
articles.summary: Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who both spent time in NFL training camps, were left off LSU's Week 1 roster despite a judge saying they were eligible to...
articles.body:
When it comes to LSU's decision to leave two former NFL players off its roster , Lane Kiffin says he is looking at the big picture.

In an appearance on ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday, Kiffin spoke about the choice to not include Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris in the Tigers' lineup for Saturday's game against Clemson.

Wright and Harris, who both spent time in NFL training camps before they were cut, were ruled eligible to play by a judge on Thursday, in a big legal win for LSU. But on Saturday, Kiffin said that the decision to omit them was in "the best interest of the team and the university" since they did not know exactly what consequences could befall the team if they played.

"That wasn't easy. As much as I feel for the players, and I believe that you fight for what you believe in, and I believe that, you know, these kids have an opportunity to play, just like all of the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters," Kiffin said. "But the same time, I'm the head coach at LSU and I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could've come by adding them to the roster."

Those "uncertainties" likely stemmed from LSU's ongoing feud with the SEC. The SEC, along with other power conferences, banned the inclusion of players who had signed professional contracts . However, unlike the other conferences, the SEC was also considering some very steep penalties for schools and players that violated that ban, including boycotting LSU games and sanctions against the school, such as probation or expulsion.

The SEC also filed a federal lawsuit against LSU on Thursday, alleging that the Tigers "waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes to play football for LSU."

Wright and Harris both played for Ole Miss before leaving for the NFL. Both went undrafted; Harris signed with the New Orleans Saints in May, and Wright spent time with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns. The players were cut before training camp ended, prompting them to follow their old coach to LSU.

The ongoing college eligibility crisis stems from the NCAA adopting its new "five-for-five" rule, which gives college players five years of eligibility in a five-year span. The class of 2022 was not eligible for this rule change, leaving many athletes in that class to go to court.

When speaking on "College GameDay," Kiffin said that the members of his team were not distracted by the whole saga.

"They're in a great place," Kiffin said, via The Athletic . "All this stuff is made in the media; you guys have to cover it, I have to answer it, but these guys don't worry about it. They've got a team that they've been with this whole time. They said, 'Hey, coach, if we can add some players to help us win, let's go.' That's my job to always look at those things, but this team is ready to go; they've prepared a lot for this moment."

Kiffin, meanwhile, seems to be fine with his role as a college football villain.

"A lot of times to do great things, you are going to be hated," Kiffin said .

articles.title: El Fulham de Arbeloa, tocado: remontada del Palace y tercera derrota en Premier
articles.standfirst: Los de Arbeloa, en descenso a Championship... pese al gol de Palacios
articles.summary: Los de Arbeloa, en descenso a Championship... pese al gol de Palacios
articles.body: No es el arranque de 'era Arbeloa' que los hinchas del Fulham soñaban en Craven Cottage. Pese a la victoria en Copa de la Liga (ante el Wimbledon de League One), son tres derrotas en tres partidos de Premier League. La última, este sábado en casa... ante un Crystal Palace que remontó. Y eso que no fue un mal partido del Fulham. Al revés, de hecho; fueron superiores. Pero a los londinenses les faltó eficacia de cara al arco rival (pese a los dos tantos que anotaron) y sufrieron mucho en defensa contra un Palace que anotó tres goles en cinco disparos a puerta. En el aire quedó el gol de César Palacios. El canterano del Real Madrid hizo el 2-1 aprovechando una buena acción de un Joshua King estelar que también había hecho el 1-0. Pero Tyrick Mitchell anuló cualquier ilusión que pudiera sobrevolar Craven Cottage. El inglés firmó doblete (el 2-2, con bastante fortuna tras un despeje de Gonzalo) y arrancó una remontada que certificó Chilwell en el 77'. De nuevo, tras una acción rocambolesca y mal defendida por el Fulham. A Arbeloa se le pone, por lo tanto, muy cuesta arriba el arranque de Premier. Y más aún con lo que viene: Anfield... y el Liverpool de Andoni Iraola. Luego, el Manchester United en el Cottage. Y necesitan sumar.

images.caption: Álvaro Arbeloa, llegando al estadio para el Fulham - Palace. FULHAM.

articles.title: El Girona luce poderío en El Molinón y endosa al Sporting la primera derrota
articles.standfirst: Una genialidad de Asprilla y otra del debutante Carles Pérez deciden en El Molinón; a los asturianos no les sirve su empuje en la segunda parte
articles.summary: Una genialidad de Asprilla y otra del debutante Carles Pérez deciden en El Molinón; a los asturianos no les sirve su empuje en la segunda parte
articles.body: El Girona ha dado un golpe de autoridad y un aviso a todos sus rivales con una victoria en El Molinón que muestra la capacidad que tiene su plantilla. Un golazo del pichichi Asprilla en la primera parte y otro del debutante Carles Pérez en la segunda, cuando mejor estaba el Sporting, fueron definitivos para encadenar su segunda victoria consecutiva. Por contra los asturianos sufren así su primera derrota liguera. Sin complejos y con la moral al alza después de sus victorias en la última jornada, dos en el caso asturiano, afrontaron el choque. Sobre todo el Girona, que comenzó mandón y advirtiendo constantemente con Asprilla por banda derecha. Guille Rosas fue el primero en intentarlo con un disparo con la zurda que salió cerca de la escuadra, pero el control y la amenaza era gerundense. Pese a ello, el conjunto rojiblanco estaba relativamente cómodo sin balón, pero expuesto al fallo. Fue así como de un balón largo de Gazzaniga llegó el tanto. Asprilla se coló entre los defensores, controló orientado de espuela y ante Rubén Yáñez, desubicado el portero, picó el balón para el 0-1 antes de la media hora. Acción de talento del colombiano como error grosero del Sporting. El tanto equilibró las cosas. Los de Quique Álvarez moderaron su valentía y los de Larcamón, poco a poco, fueron asumiendo la responsabilidad de buscar algo más. Gelabert, desaparecido hasta entonces, comenzó a aparecer y Juan Otero, más generoso que nunca, desaprovechó un gran centro de Duñabeitia para el empate en el añadido. Ya en la reanudación, con Sarco por Konrad y Pyshchur por Vanat, los locales fueron a más. Nikita Iosifov advertía, Sarco hacía daño entre líneas, pero las ocasiones no llegaban salvo una de Andrés Cuenca que salvó Gazzaniga. Por eso, Nicolás Larcamón se fue al ataque, dando entrada al debutante Casas y apostando por un 4-4-2. La valentía no tuvo premio y el talento tiró de lógica. Así fue como Carles Pérez, que también debutaba, regateó con la mirada a Pablo Vázquez y batió a Rubén Yáñez sin problemas con un disparo cruzado ajustado al poste. La sentencia en el 75’. Demasiado castigo para el Sporting, que incluso rozó el gol con Loum y Casas poco antes del 90’. Poderoso caballero es Don Dinero. El Girona tiene más recursos, esa fue la clave de esta tarde.

images.caption: Asprilla, autor del 0-1, golpea al balón ante Corredera LALIGA
David López, Francés y Fran Beltrán felicitan a Gazzaniga por su asistencia en el 0-1 LALIGA

articles.title: Alineaciones probables del partido de LaLiga del Valencia vs Barça
articles.standfirst: Flick medita cambios pensando en la Champions y Corberán mantendrá una línea de cinco defensas con muchas bajas por lesión
articles.summary: Flick medita cambios pensando en la Champions y Corberán mantendrá una línea de cinco defensas con muchas bajas por lesión
articles.body: Barcelona y Valencia se cruzan este domingo en Mestalla, a las 16:15 horas. Hansi Flick tiene altas importantes mientras que Carlos Corberán encara el encuentro marcado por las ausencias. El técnico culé hará cambios en su alineación: ya afronta un calendario tan apretado como exigente. El Barça tiene las bajas por lesión de De Jong y Roony, pero Hansi Flick puede disponer ya de Gavi, superada la contusión que sufrió en Elche y que le obligó a no estar disponible contra el Athletic y el Rayo. El preparador germano cuenta, además, con las altas de Livakovic y Gabriel Jesus, últimos fichajes culés. El técnico no descartó incluso que el brasileño disfrute de algunos minutos en Mestalla y debute así con la camiseta culé. El preparador azulgrana medita hacer cambios esta jornada en el once, ya que el miércoles se estrena en la Champions League: recibe al Feyenoord en el Spotify Camp Nou. Las variaciones pueden afectar a todas las líneas, y hombres como Cancelo, Christensen, Rodri y Adeyemi pueden ser protagonistas. El Valencia, por su parte, llega al encuentro de Mestalla marcado por las bajas por lesión. Corberán no podrá disponer de Luis Rioja, Guido Rodríguez, Copete, Sadiq, Justin de Haas, Foulquier y los lesionados de larga duración Canós y Diego López. Por este motivo, no tiene mucho margen tras el desastroso partido en Riazor. Cuenta con un refuerzo de nivel, Harvey Elliot, que ya se refirió en su presentación oficial al excesivo calor en los entrenamientos, y que apunta a debutar, pero desde el banquillo. Corberán ha trabajado durante la semana con tres centrales, aunque la duda está en si mete a Pepelu en esa línea de tres de la retaguardia (con lo que Dieng sería titular) o lo deja como pivote para mantener a Arnau Martínez, Tárrega y Diakhaby. Alineación probable del Valencia: Dimitrievski; Maffeo, Arnau, Pepelu, Diakhaby, Jesús Vázquez; Ugrinic, Guerra, Dieng, Sato; y Danjuma. Alineación probable del Barcelona: Joan García; Cancelo, Christensen, Cubarsí; Espart; Rodri, Bernal; Adeyemi, Fermín, Raphinha y Gordon.

articles.title: Con esta defensa lo de Julián pasa a un segundo plano
articles.body: Calentaba Julián minutos antes de arrancar el gran choque de San Mamés. El argentino, siempre arropado por su amigo Cuti, empezaba en un campo histórico como el del Athletic su particular redención. Sabe que su situación no es sencilla pese a que ya cerró el mercado de pases y que tiene mucho que remar... La Araña saltó al campo a la hora. En un cuádruple cambio histórico apareció el argentino justo cuando el Atlético se había desangrado. Y es que el 19 apareció (a los 10 minutos casi marca un gol que le sacó Unai) después de que la defensa de los de Simeone concediera dos de esos tantos que impiden luchar por cotas grandes. Y esto debe preocupar más todavía que cómo solucionar el enrevesado asunto de Julián. Y ya es decir... Un minuto tardó el Athletic en destrozar al Atlético en el arranque de la segunda parte. Un minuto en el que los tantos de Nico y Robert Navarro dejaron retratado a la defensa rojiblanca, pero especialmente a un Grimaldo al que le costará borrar las dos acciones. La primera, por estar fuera de sitio (tuvo que salir Hancko). La segunda, por el regate que se comió antes del gol. Llegaba el tiempo casi al descanso cuando Unai Simón tenía el esférico controlado. A la presión fue un Baena que amagó con darle una patada.. y luego le lanzó un gesto cariñoso al compañero de selección. Dos campeones del mundo, un gesto de complicidad que no gustó a todo San Mamés, que silbó en parte la 'broma' del 10 del Atlético. Baena, por cierto, cada vez tiene más galones y valentía en este equipo. Intentó un gol desde el medio del campo que habría sido el tanto de lo que va de LaLiga. Hace dos temporadas fueron decisivos para que el Athletic se metiera en la Champions. Hablamos de Sancet y Nico Wiliams, a los que el bajón del curso pasado por las lesiones acabó pasando factura a los de San Mamés. De hecho, de su buen nivel depende de que los de Bilbao vuelvan a plantar cara a equipos como el Atlético, el Madrid y el Barça. El 10 abrió el marcador con un gran tanto de cabeza. El 8 puso el 3-0 para cerrar la goleada local. A las 16.43, minuto 25 del partido, llegó la pausa de hidratación. Necesaria no, imprescindible, una vez que el termómetro superaba los 30 grados y los jugadores sufrían con una sensación térmica insufrible también en la grada. A los que ponen los horarios les importa poco, pero no eran las mejores condiciones para jugar un gran partido de fútbol. Precioso homenaje al equipo del Athletic campeón del mundo Genuine de jugadores con discapacidad intelectual. San Mamés se puso en pie para darles la ovación de la tarde y todos los futbolistas de los dos equipos les dieron una merecida ovación. Seguro que jamás olvidan este 5 de septiembre. Un aplauso inmenso para ellos.

images.caption: Iñaki, en una acción ante el Atlético.

articles.title: Simeone: "El Athletic aprovechó esos dos minutos de desconexión, es responsabilidad del cuerpo técnico"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Atlético analizó el partido ante el Athletic.
articles.summary: El entrenador del Atlético analizó el partido ante el Athletic.
articles.body: Diego Pablo Simeone atendió a los medios en San Mamés tras el encuentro ante el Athletic en el que los del Metropolitano encajaron la primera derrota del curso. Falta de concentración al entrar en la segunda parte. El partido es lo que se vio. Un buen primer tiempo y dos minutos de poca atención y resolución de situaciones que debimos resolver mejor. El Athletic aprovechó ese momento de desconexión. Ganaron el partido justamente. Qué le duele más: la derrota o la desconexión El partido estaba siendo muy bueno de cara al segundo tiempo. Pero no resolvimos bien en dos minutos, pero responsabilidad del cuerpo técnico por no darle la situación para que lo resolvieran. Motivo de la desconexión El cuerpo técnico no pudo transmitir lo que necesitaban. Más esperanzado por la primera parte o por lo de la segunda Estamos en construcción del equipo. Vamos a atravesar situaciones complejas. Empezamos bien, pero estos dos minutos de hoy nos dieron un golpe para reaccionar. Julián no salió a calentar después ¿En serio? No tengo nada que comentar. Defensa del Athletic Conocemos a su entrenador y tiene las cosas claras. Salvo la de Julián no tuvimos ocasiones claras. El Athletic va a pelear por los primeros lugares.

articles.title: Aberdeen 0-0 Kilmarnock: Teams fail to find target in tetchy contest at Pittodrie as both sides end losing streaks
articles.summary: Report and highlights as the 10 men of Kilmarnock hold on for point against similarly out-of-form Aberdeen; first of two quick meetings between the clubs as they face each other in Premier Sports Cup next weekend
articles.body:
Quality chances were at a premium with Aberdeen's Tony Yogane hitting the inside of the post in the first half but Dons goalkeeper Marius Muller was the busier goalkeeper throughout.

Aaron Tshibola saw red for the visitors for a second booking with eight minutes remaining but Aberdeen were unable to capitalise on the extra man.

In the first of a double-header between the sides, they meet again at Rugby Park in the Premier Sports Cup next weekend, both were looking to arrest poor league form.

Aberdeen had not scored in their previous three league games, having only taken points from their opening day win over Hearts at Pittodrie.

Killie had lost all four of their Premiership matches so far, and were keen to avoid becoming the first side to lose their first five of the season - the last having been current Killie boss Neil McCann's Dundee side in 2018.

Both managers made changes, with Aberdeen making four after the defeat at Celtic in midweek, and McCall swapping three after the loss to St Mirren.

The home side showed some smart early initiative as Stuart Armstrong and Kevin Nisbet combined to create an opening after just two minutes, but Armstrong opted for an extra pass and the chance was gone.

Killie captain Greg Kiltie flashed wide of the left-hand upright from 20 yards, before, midway through the first half, Aberdeen's Nesta Guinness-Walker threw himself in front of a Jamie Brandon effort after Mitchy Ntelo gave away possession cheaply in midfield.

Aberdeen moved Lewis Smith infield and he flashed an effort over the bar, before Yogane curled an effort off the inside of the far post after cutting inside from a Smith pass.

Muller pushed another Kiltie effort past the far post and Aberdeen's Dan Happe saw a header held by Max Stryjek as the first half drew to a close.

The home side made a triple change at the interval, switching to a 3-4-1-2 formation, and soon after sub Toyosi Olusanya just failed to connect with a ball across goal which was put wide by Smith at the back post.

That sparked a period of pressure that saw an Ayoub Mouloua header held by Stryjek, after McCann had been booked following a VAR review of a potential handball in the Killie box.

Armstrong saw an effort from distance held, before Muller pushed a Cathal McCarthy header over and then impressively denied Kiltie from point-blank range.

Tshibola was denied by the masked Muller, the goalkeeper diving high to his left to push a 25-yard free-kick over.

Ten minutes from time, good hold-up play from Mouloua created an opening for Chris Cadden, his effort blocked by a sliding challenge from George Stanger.

Killie were reduced to 10 men when Tshibola was dismissed for a challenge on Mats Knoester, having been booked for a first-half foul on Smith.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Brentford 1-1 Sunderland: Enzo Le Fee penalty cancels out Vitaly Janelt opener but Bees' unbeaten start continues
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Brentford drew 1-1 with Sunderland; Vitaly Janelt scored a well-taken opener but Enzo Le Fee's penalty drew the visitors level; Brentford remain unbeaten in the Premier League and have moved into fifth following the point
articles.body:
The Bees broke the deadlock just before the hour mark thanks to Vitaly Janelt's well-taken effort into the top left corner, only for referee Thomas Bramall to point to the spot in the 82nd minute to penalise Keane Lewis-Potter for holding Wilson Isidor inside the box.

Latest news and rumours: Brentford | Sunderland

The full-back did not have eyes on the ball while making contact and after being confirmed by VAR, Le Fee stepped up to dispatch it into the bottom right corner.

"We can do better, I always look at us," Brentford boss Keith Andrews said in his post-match press conference.

"I wasn't bowled over with the officiating today, though, which I rarely say.

"I don't tend to go on about officials too much. I will talk myself into trouble but I didn't like the flow of the game; there were incidents where it was not under control."

A point marked a fair return for both sides in a game where momentum swung in favour of both teams at different stages of the contest.

Sunderland, who switched to a back five for this fixture, had started the better side and came close to an opener in the first half after Dan Ballard's goal was disallowed following a lengthy VAR review and Le Fee hit the post with a fierce strike from range.

"It is a shame," Regis Le Bris said after the game regarding Ballard's goal, which was ruled out due to debutant Kevin Danso being offside. "If you need four and a half minutes to make a decision, it means you are hesitating."

Half-time changes from Keith Andrews - replacing Michael Kayode, Mamadou Sangare and Dango Ouattara with Aaron Hickey, Yehor Yarmoliuk and Anthony - inspired fresh impetus going forward.

Their unbeaten start to the season continues but marks the second consecutive week the Bees have squandered a lead late on and were forced to settle for a point following the 1-1 at Leeds United last time out.

9: DISALLOWED! Ballard's opener ruled out due to Danso offside on debut

20: OFF THE POST! Le Fee strikes the post with emphatic volley

45: TRIPLE CHANGE! Andrews replaces Kayode, Ouattara and Sangare with Hickey, Yarmoliuk and Anthony

57: GOAL! Janelt scores the opener with well-taken effort into top corner

70: DISALLOWED! Anthony's tap-in ruled out for foul on Roefs

82: PENALTY! Le Fee scores equaliser after Lewis-Potter penalised for foul on Isidor

"It had a lot in it, the game. In the first half, we didn't hit the levels we had. The way they played was very good.

"We were a little bit off it and in the second half we did the basics very well. It allowed us to have control and more territory; we looked more like us and got ourselves in front.

"There were then decisions that went for us and did not go for us.

"I knew it would be a very difficult game today. It was a proper game. If I am in the stand and watching from afar, it is what the Premier League is all about. Going toe-to-toe with a good team and good coach."

Le Bris: We dominated but Brentford switched the momentum

"First half, we were dominant and created four big chances in the first 30 minutes.

"We managed this part of the game but didn't score. It is always a big shame.

"They changed three players and it switched the momentum. They scored but the lads were still in the game.

"We know we are good when we are behind. The subs helped."

VAR dominates post-match discussions again

A miss for both teams with VAR at the forefront of the post-match discussions once again.

Brentford boss Keith Andrews was right to criticise the flow of the game and the control Thomas Bramall had at times but zero questions can be raised about the penalty.

A greater emphasis is being placed on players who do not look at the ball, have both hands on their opponent, make no attempt to play the ball or commit sustained holding of their opponent.

Keane Lewis-Potter did all four in plain sight of match officials and VAR.

Sunderland, meanwhile, were also left with a bitter taste in their mouths regarding officiating after it took longer than four minutes to disallow Dan Ballard's goal in the ninth minute.

"It's a shame because if you need four and a half minutes to make your decision, it means that you are hesitating," Regis Le Bris said after the game.

"So it wasn't a decision for us. It is what it is."

An enthralling game where momentum swung both ways should leave us talking about in-game management, the finish of Vitaly Janelt and Enzo Le Fee's late equaliser. Instead, it's VAR again.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: West Bromwich Albion 1-0 Watford: Jimmy-Jay Morgan nets winner for Baggies
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between West Bromwich Albion and Watford at The Hawthorns on Saturday; Jimmy-Jay Morgan scores the only goal as Baggies claim narrow in.
articles.body:
The 20-year-old, a £1.3million summer signing, scored in the 36th minute for his third Championship strike and first at The Hawthorns to extend Albion's unbeaten home record to 10 matches.

It was a game of two halves, with Morgan denied twice and Aune Heggebo once in the first half, while Watford missed two chances after the break.

Watford are now winless away from home in their last nine trips, since February.

Intense pressing on Albion's midfield saw Watford threaten first when Othmane Maamma forced goalkeeper Max O'Leary into a vital block with his leg.

Maamma's opportunity came when Hector Kyprianou dispossessed Ousmane Diakite and Martin Payero ran from deep before slipping in the Moroccan forward to his right.

Albion responded when Morgan's low shot was blocked by goalkeeper Federico Ravaglia after Chris Mepham's long pass into the striker.

Albion had the ball in the net in the 34th minute, but Morgan appeared to head the ball out of Ravaglia's hands from Nolan Galves' deflected cross and it was disallowed for a foul.

The cheers were somewhat muted but the booking for Morgan seemed harsh.

But the hosts did not have long to wait to break the deadlock.

Morgan tapped home Harry Whitwell's cutback after the latter burst into the box from Isaac Price's cross in the 36th minute.

Watford, who introduced Edo Kayembe for left-back Jordan Zemura at half-time, twice threatened soon after the restart.

Spaniard Iker Bravo's first-time shot was blocked from Luca Kjerrumgaard's cross.

Then Payero hooked over the bar from close range after Maamma headed down Edoardo Bove's deep cross at the far post.

Whitwell was showing his potential and Kayembe was booked for wrestling him to the ground as he charged down the right in the 63rd minute.

Watford threatened again when Bravo could only glance weakly straight at O'Leary from Keben's inviting centre.

But Albion missed the chance to double their lead in the 71st minute.

Whitwell slid Heggebo clean through with a lovely reverse pass and the Norway striker tried to lift his shot over Ravaglia only for the keeper to smuggle it behind for a corner.

Substitute Stephy Mavididi had the chance to level it but the forward blazed high over the bar after twisting inside his marker on the angle.

Albion appeared to be denied a penalty at the death when substitute Felix Horn Myhre seemed to be pushed over on the ball from Keben.

In a melee seconds later, Bravo was booked after pushing substitute Jayson Molumby in the corner.

"I challenged him before the game - it was his third match in a week so can he do it? You could see it in his pressing because it was a different side to him with the amount of blocks he made.

"I'm surprised really by how good he is. It's credit to the recruitment team really for finding him.

"It's really good work by them and it shows there are players out there. The question was 'could he step up?', but he has answered that brilliantly.

"He looks comfortable but we just need to keep on with his work rate. He's proved he can do it. The challenge for him is 'can he maintain that level?' but I believe he can do it.

"He has that youthfulness and freshness and he's a little cocky as well. Those ones will go far. He has that swagger and I quite like it."

"We deserved a draw but if you don't score, it's impossible to win.

"We showed the right mentality but the result was negative.

"We played well but we know it's important for us to arrive in the box better to find a positive result.

"West Brom away is not easy but my team stayed competitive for 90 minutes."

Injury-hit Watford are without four full-backs which forced Albert Eames into his full league debut at right-back.

Midfielder Edo Kayembe came on at half-time at left-back after Jordan Zemura hurt his knee.

Dionisi added: "It's not easy at the moment. But we knew this was the situation with eight games including the Carabao Cup until the international break."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: See the FSU running back that got a boost in College Football 27
articles.body:
FSU may not be the highest-rated team in EA Sports' College Football 27, but that doesn't mean love isn't being given to some of their better players.

In CFB 27, and by a broader extension, sports video games, the players within are defined by their "overall", a general number that takes into account how good all of their individual attributes are to give a rough idea without needing to dive too deep into analytics.

Yes, that means Ohio State and Georgia are on top of the world and have a lot of high overall players, given the program's reputation and star talent. Florida State , meanwhile, despite only being an 82 overall this season, has been underrated for a while. Until now.

Ousmane Kromah had his overall rating bumped up from an 84 to an 85 overall thanks to his performance against New Mexico State. His stiff arm increased by three points, while his trucking and carry abilities increased by one.

Kromah is now the fifth-best player on FSU, behind Daniel Lyons, Xavier Chaplin, Quintrevion Wisner, and Duce Robinson.

College Football 27 is available on PS5, Xbox Series X and S, and for the first time, on PC through Steam and the Epic Games Store. You can view every ACC team's rating here .

Contact/Follow us @FSUWire on X, and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of FSU news, notes, and opinions. Jacob Smith is a contributor for FSU Wire, part of the USA TODAY Network. You can also follow Jacob on X at @jsmith_sports .

articles.title: Schalke vs. FC Bayern: Gamethread
articles.summary: FC Bayern takes on Schalke for the first time in three years
articles.body:
72' — Pavlović goes into the referee's notebook.

68' — Olise went down in the box, penalty not given.

64' — Laimer found himself in space but his shot hit the side netting.

58' — Gosens could not score on one end, while Díaz did the same at the other end. Karius made several big saves to deny Bayern.

56' — Michael Olise and Jamal Musiala replace Ismael Saibari and Lennart Karl.

55' — Tah's header off a corner goes well over the bar.

54' — Díaz is played through but his chip shot is cleared off the line.

50' — Aleksandar Pavlović commits a foul after knocking a Schalke player over.

48' — Schalke stop Díaz in his tracks again.

46' — Second half time. Let's get going! Harry Kane comes on for Nathaniel Brown.

For the most part, Bayern has been sloppy in the first half. Lots of misplaced passes, dangerous runs that went unnoticed, and wasted set pieces.

It's not like Bayern is devoid of ideas in attack, Schalke just happened to be more than equal to it.

Credit to the home side for giving Bayern a headache; the visitors had great difficulty in making attacking forays into opposition territory.

45+3' — A loose pass from Díaz nearly cost Bayern a goal, but Tah managed to snuff out the danger. The referee has also blown for halftime.

45' — Two minutes of stoppage time are added on.

42' — Bayern win a free kick just outside the Schalke box.

41' — Brown slips Díaz in, but he couldn't get the shot away.

39' — Upamecano prevents a Schalke player from having a shot. Bayern goal kick.

38' — Schalke's counterattack fizzles out.

36' — The ensuing free kick from Schalke is parried away by Manuel Neuer.

35' — Upamecano lost possession and had to commit a tactical foul; the Frenchman is booked.

31' — Upamecano is tackled by Junior Dina Ebimbe who gets a yellow card.

30' — Saibari shoots a loose ball over the Schalke goal.

29' — Gosens turns Ismael Saibari's cross behind for a corner.

26' — Brown's corner is collected by Karius.

24' — A handball is called against Dayot Upamecano but the referee says it's not a handball.

21' — Karl is dispossessed which earn Schalke a goal kick.

19' — Schalke's free kick comes to nothing after Bayern cleared the ball.

18' — Konrad Laimer goes into Robin Gosens which earns Schalke a free kick.

16' — Karius safely collects the corner from Joshua Kimmich.

13' — Lorius Karius denies Nathaniel Brown inside the box. Bayern corner.

8' — Alphonso Davies receives the ball on the left wing, and his intended cross nearly ended up in the net.

7' — Jonathan Tah collides with a Schalke player. Play is waved on.

5' — Luis Díaz beats three players inside the Schalke box but the hosts clear the ball.

Lineups are out! The starting XI welcomes back familiar faces like Alphonso Davies, Lennart Karl and Dayot Upamecano. Manuel Neuer trots out on his return to his boyhood club, while Ismael Saibari is handed a first ever Bundesliga start. Harry Kane and Michael Olise are both benched, while Jamal Musiala starts alongside them.

Bayern Munich went three for three to start the 2026/27 season, beating Borussia Dortmund (2-1 in the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup), VfB Stuttgart (5-1, Bundesliga Matchday 1), and VfL Osnabrück (DFB-Pokal, round 2). Today, they travel to North Rhine-Westphalia to visit old foes Schalke 04.

Die Königsblauen is back better than ever, though their return to the Bundesliga got off to a rocky start with a 3-0 defeat to Augsburg. Schalke did win against Hallescher in the Pokal, requiring extra time to seal progression to the next round.

Schalke hasn't beaten Bayern in 15 years; Bayern themselves have only lost thrice in nearly 70 Bundesliga games under Vincent Kompany. The odds are stacked against Schalke, but if there's one thing about football, it's that you shouldn't rule anyone out.

Location : Veltins-Arena, Gelsenkirchen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany

Kickoff : 6:30 PM Local time | 12:30 PM EST | 9:30 AM PST

TV/streaming: Peacock (en español), USA/Fandango (United States — check listings) , Find Your Country

articles.title: Fernandez and Ndiaye show signs of promise on Man City debuts
articles.summary: Manchester City gave £185m of deadline-day talent their Premier League debuts in the win over Coventry - and manager Enzo Maresca will have enjoyed what he s...
articles.body:
Manchester City gave £185m worth of talent signed on transfer deadline day their Premier League debuts in the 1-0 Premier League victory over Coventry and manager Enzo Maresca will have been quietly satisfied with what he saw from his new duo.

Midfielder Enzo Fernandez, brought in from Chelsea for £125m, was initially named as a substitute but was given a late call-up into the starting XI after Nico O'Reilly sustained a knock in the warm-up, while £60m Iliman Ndiaye also played from the off.

Both players have had limited time on the training ground with their new team-mates, but showcased early signs of what they will bring to the side and how competition for starting places has ramped up at Etihad Stadium.

Maresca knows Fernandez from his time in charge at Chelsea, with the pair winning the Europa Conference League and Club World Cup together, and he played a pivotal role in Erling Haaland's winning goal.

Maresca said: "It is much more easier when a player you already share time together [joins] because they know exactly what you want.

"We know each other very well, I know how good he is and I know that he is going to help the team to win games."

Players will 'learn how we want them to play'

City clung on to a nervy victory against the Sky Blues to maintain their 100% winning start to the season, but managed to get the job done courtesy of a string of saves from goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Haaland continued his fine start to the season by converting his third goal in as many games from Antoine Semenyo's deep cross, which came after Fernandez played through a slide-rule pass to the Ghanaian.

Playing in the number eight role, Argentina international Fernandez was given licence to roam and make late bursts into the box - he touched the ball six times in the opposition area, with only Haaland managing more with 11.

Fernandez could have had a dream debut but saw two shots blocked, before being replaced after 76 minutes by fellow summer signing Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international was part of City's midfield rebuild and highlights the options available to Maresca despite the departures of Bernardo Silva, Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez.

Ndiaye, meanwhile, became the first Senegalese player to represent City and is bound to give opposition defenders with his trickery and pace. No player attempted more dribbles in the match than his eight.

Maresca said: "Enzo and Iliman [played their] first game with us and then Ayyoub and Ryan [McAidoo] their first game in front of our fans.

"That is why I said there are many reasons I am happy about our win. I think they were all good.

"Ili just had two sessions with us. He needs to understand how to move. Most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, wrong position, but he needs to learn and for sure he is going to learn."

Asked to elaborate on Ndiaye's performance, Maresca said: "When Marc Guehi has the ball and he was dropping a lot and we don't need that.

"We need him in the last third so he can be a little bit more higher. That space was more for Josko Gvardiol.

"It is the same thing in this [other] side. But it is normal and with time they will learn the way we want them to play."

City's deadline-day deals make it easy to forget that England international Elliot Anderson also joined this summer for £116m from Nottingham Forest.

The 23-year-old is beginning to find his feet in a City shirt, being named man of the match against Coventry despite the travelling team threatening to cause a huge upset.

Frank Lampard's side could not take their chances and Anderson ended the game completing 143 of his 155 passes, four more than the Coventry team.

"Really impressed," said Maresca. "Not just today. He was very good against Palace; he was also very good against Bournemouth, having only been one week with us when we changed him for cramp.

"But the best thing with Elliot is the day by day. He is asking how he can learn. We sit with him one-v-one video [analysis] and he wants to be better, and that is the best thing for any player."

Former England international Lampard added: "He is a really good player. I admire him from afar and did at Forest, but this was the first time I had seen him close up in the flesh.

"Very smart, very talented and a very good player - good brain, everything you need in a midfield player - and he is going to be a fantastic player for Manchester City.

"He had a lot of the ball today. I don't think he could hurt us, but he was constantly on it and I highly respect players like that, no doubt."
authors: Shamoon Hafez - Manchester City reporter at Etihad Stadium

articles.title: Takeaways: Atlético lapse into old habits as Athletic ease to victory
articles.summary: Notes of last season came through strong following disaster in Bilbao
articles.body:
Are we really doing this all over again?

Atlético Madrid 's desperately poor 3-0 loss to Athletic Club in at San Mamés brought up familiar ghosts from seasons gone by, leaving fans questioning if anything has actually changed ahead of Wednesday's UEFA Champions League trip to Anfield.

A lack of intensity away from home and a vulnerable left side saw Atleti rue missed chances in the first half, before completely capitulating immediately from the restart in the second.

Here are Into the Calderón's key takeaways from this first loss of the 2026/27 season.

Atleti are making me sound like a broken record with no other ways of analysing one of their matches at this point. For the best part of two seasons, I have been using the analogy of a pool table on uneven ground to describe the way that the entirety of the team's play seems to gently drift over the right side of the pitch, and it's getting tiring.

The trouble with having two explosively quick touchline-hugging players, and a left-footed attacker who wants to start their moves from a position to allow them to cut inside, is that eventually everyone will find themselves standing on each other's toes. It becomes very predictable for the opposition to know how to set themselves up. I assumed the idea of having Kang-In Lee in the team would be to award Marcos Llorente the freedom of the wing, with the option of introducing Giuliano Simeone as a pairing with Marc Pubill when he plays right-back instead. Yet it turns out that Llorente, Giuliano and Kang-In are all looking like they'll play (for now at least), leaving the 'guys who try and make stuff happen' all bunched up together.

A heavy right side usually results in a light left side, something so painful to think about going through for another season. Poor Ademola Lookman already received an apology from Diego Simeone on matchday 1 for playing him out of position, and is now cutting an isolated figure once more in the barren, deserted land of the left wing. Whenever the ball did find its way out there, the Nigerian was expected to make something happen out of nothing, often starting with the ball in a standing position tasked with finding a way through a well-organised Athletic defense all by himself. That's not going to happen. He needs people to play off and an associate to combine with. Get the boy a striker and see what happens.

I'd like to take this opportunity to comment on how the promotion of Lookman's understudy from the regionalised third tier of Spanish football is one I do not understand. This is nothing against Arnau Ortiz, I think he's a fine man, a good football player and someone who was fun to watch for Atlético Madrileño last season in their quest to go up a division to professional football. However for him to be a revulsivo off the bench in a game where the team is chasing a deficit of two goals is a damning indictment of where the squad currently finds itself. Ortiz is also 24 years old which doesn't even leave him the excuse of being a promising young talent. He'd be a fine addition to a mid-to-bottom table club in LALIGA, not a Champions League aspirant.

Defensively on that flank, Alejandro Grimaldo is the only true left-back in the squad — Matteo Ruggeri and Julio Díaz were offloaded in the summer transfer window, and Dani Martínez can play there, but he too is devoid of any kind of first division experience — making the part (or lack of) he played in all three of today's goals a worrying sign of things to come. The World Cup winner was dragged into no man's land for Nico Williams' opener, torn a new one by Robert Navarro a minute later and slow to react to the counterattack down his side for Oihan Sancet's third. Failure to secure another left-back on deadline day might prove to come back and haunt Atleti, with fingers ready to point at Mateu Alemany if that's the case.

Max Rushden of The Guardian often talks about good kicks of the football. How the essence of this sport is to propel the round thing with the body part that hangs off the end of your leg.

My word, Atleti have some good kickers of the football. The way Kang-In Lee gets his head down and carries the ball on both feet around the pitch is wonderful to watch. Álex Baena can hit one, gosh. It gives me great pleasure to watch Pablo Barrios pass and dribble. I'm sure once Grimaldo remembers how to cross and shoot we will marvel at his ability to do so.

However, for all the technical brilliance that this Atlético Madrid team possesses, they were ultimately torn apart by the intensity of an Athletic Club side who (forgive me for digging the old cliché out) simply wanted it more.

There were early signs toward the end of the first half when Atleti looked to have become slightly complacent after missing two good opportunities to go ahead. The home side turned up the heat on the hob by one number, the San Mamés crowd responded with a fiery gust of support and all of a sudden Simeone's team was on the back foot.

That momentum was preserved during the interval and Athletic came flying out of the blocks in the second period, allowing Atleti no time to execute their idea of controlling the game. The ball was in play for just 43 seconds before there was a two-goal margin between the teams, and the typically-tall order of winning in this legendary Spanish footballing setting suddenly became a whole lot harder.

With a game to chase and an opposition out for yet more blood, Los Rojiblancos looked frail and went back into the shell we have seen them crawl into away from the Metropolitano for a couple of years now. A brief spell of looking as if something may happen did occur, but then the substitutes only added to the disjointed nature of the team's performance.

I do hope this was merely a blip and that the away performances are going to be more like what we saw at Sevilla last week.

Julián did his best impression of caring

Nothing more to say for now. When he scores and holds his hands up to the fans, there will be more to add.

articles.title: Lens lose again ahead of Champions League date
articles.summary: Lens's difficult start to the new season continued on Saturday as Mamadou Kone scored his first Ligue 1 goal to give Lorient a 1-0 win at last season's runne...
articles.body:
Lens's difficult start to the new season continued on Saturday as Mamadou Kone scored his first Ligue 1 goal to give Lorient a 1-0 win at last season's runners-up.

After Lens sold several key players and lost their coach in the close season, new boss Dino Toppmoeller started brightly by beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions' Trophy and then opening the Ligue 1 campaign with a 5-2 win over Auxerre.

But that was followed by a defeat at Strasbourg and now this second consecutive reverse.

Kone pounced on a loose ball on 54 minutes to score the only goal of the game.

Ahead of their trip to Slavia Prague for a Champions League game on Thursday, Lens showed little fight against an abrasive Lorient.

Le Havre play Brest while Nice host Le Mans later Saturday.
